title: Quasi-compact restriction of a kernel pair
statement:
Let $\mathcal E$ be a Grothendieck topos presented on a small site, in the universes of [def-weil-size-convention], with quasi-compact and quasi-separated objects as in [def-trf-coherent-topos]. Let $p:P\to A$ be any morphism, put $R=P\times_A P$, and write $r_1,r_2:R\rightrightarrows P$ for its projections. Suppose $P$ is quasi-separated and $R$ is quasi-compact. For any quasi-compact objects $K,L$ and maps $k:K\to P$, $l:L\to P$, put $T=K\times_{k,P,r_1}R$, with projection $t_R:T\to R$. There is a canonical isomorphism
$$K\times_{pk,A,pl}L\ \simeq\ T\times_{r_2t_R,P,l}L.$$
It commutes with the projections to $K$ and $L$ and is natural in maps $K'\to K$, $L'\to L$ over $P$ between such objects. In a site presentation its forward map sends $(x,y)$ to $(x,(k(x),l(y)),y)$ and its inverse forgets the $R$-component. Both $T$ and $K\times_A L$ are quasi-compact. No epimorphism hypothesis on $p$, no quasi-compactness hypothesis on $P$, and no coherence hypothesis on $\mathcal E$ is required.

proof.text: Construct the forward morphism by three pullback lifts: from X = K ×_A L form the morphism to R with coordinates fst ≫ k and snd ≫ l, then lift to T, then lift to W = T ×_P L. The pullback condition in X makes the first lift well-defined, and the projection identities make the later lifts well-defined. Construct the inverse by forgetting the R coordinate: lift W → K and W → L to X, using the three pullback conditions to establish compatibility over A. By repeated pullback.hom_ext and the projection formulas the two composites are identities, yielding restrictionIso. This is the categorical universal-property version of the sectionwise formulas; it works in any category with finite limits and needs no sheaf presentation.

proof.text: The pullback lift projection formulas give all six forward and inverse coordinate identities. For morphisms a and b over P, prove naturality by successive applications of pullback.hom_ext to W, T, and R. Each resulting coordinate identity is pullback.map_fst or pullback.map_snd together with a ≫ k = k′ or b ≫ l = l′.

proof.text: Apply the defining quasi-separatedness condition of [def-trf-coherent-topos] again to T and L. This definition accepts every object equipped with a pullback square, not only the chosen pullback. Equip X with the square whose legs are restrictionIso.hom followed by the projections of W; IsPullback.of_iso_pullback proves it is a pullback. Quasi-compactness of T and L therefore gives quasi-compactness of X directly, incorporating transport across the constructed isomorphism.
